summary: charape postinstall hijacks baileys package names in the installer's node_modules
details: At `npm install` time, `scripts/postinstall.js` walks up to the installer's `node_modules` directory and unconditionally writes `package.json`, `index.js`, and `index.cjs` entry files into `@whiskeysockets/baileys`, `@adiwajshing/baileys`, and `baileys` — three package namespaces not owned by this package's author. The directory-exists check guards only `mkdir`; the entry-file writes are unconditional and overwrite any legitimate baileys install already present in the same tree. After installation, any `require('baileys')` or `require('@whiskeysockets/baileys')` by the installer or by a transitive dependency resolves to charape's code instead of the real baileys package, giving charape persistent code execution inside the installer's dependency tree. The same postinstall also writes `legacy-peer-deps=true` into the installer's project `.npmrc`, weakening dependency-resolution strictness project-wide. The hijack takes effect automatically on install with no opt-in, in contrast to the README which describes an opt-in alias via the consumer's own `package.json`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
